/-!
# Erdős Problem 1083

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1083](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1083)
- [APST04] Aronov, Boris and Pach, János and Sharir, Micha and Tardos, Gábor, *Distinct distances in
  three and higher dimensions*. Combin. Probab. Comput. (2004), 283--293.
- [CEGSW90] Clarkson, Kenneth L. and Edelsbrunner, Herbert and Guibas, Leonidas J. and Sharir, Micha
  and Welzl, Emo, *Combinatorial complexity bounds for arrangements of curves and spheres*. Discrete
  Comput. Geom. (1990), 99--160.
- [Er46b] Erdős, P., *On sets of distances of {$n$} points*. Amer. Math. Monthly (1946), 248--250.
- [SoVu08] Solymosi, József and Vu, Van H., *Near optimal bounds for the {E}rdős distinct distances
  problem in high dimensions*. Combinatorica (2008), 113--125.
-/

open Filter
open scoped EuclideanGeometry

namespace Erdos1083

/--
Let $d\geq 3$, and let $f_d(n)$ be the minimal $m$ such that every set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ determines at least $m$ distinct distances. Estimate $f_d(n)$ - in particular, is it true that $$f_d(n)=n^{\frac{2}{d}-o(1)}?$$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem erdos_1083 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ d : ℕ, 3 ≤ d → ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ, o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧
      ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
        (minimalDistinctDistances (ℝ^d) n : ℝ) = (n : ℝ) ^ ((2 : ℝ) / (d : ℝ) - o n) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1083

findings.description: The docstring defines f_d(n) as the “minimal m such that every set of n points ... determines at least m distinct distances.” Literally, the least nonnegative universally guaranteed lower bound is always 0. The Lean definition instead correctly minimizes the attained distance counts over all n-point configurations, equivalently giving the greatest universally guaranteed lower bound. This is an inherited prose typo, not a defect in the theorem's mathematical statement.
findings.source_evidence: The same wording appears at https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/1083. However, the cited primary literature makes the intended quantity unambiguous: [APST04], §1 (https://www.renyi.hu/~tardos/dimthree.pdf), defines g_d(n)=min_P g(P), with the minimum over all sets of n distinct points in d-space. [Er46b], p. 248 (https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1946-03.pdf), likewise defines the minimum number of distinct distances over point configurations.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the docstring to “the minimum number of distinct distances determined by an n-point subset of ℝ^d,” or replace “minimal m” with “maximal m.” Leave the Lean statement unchanged.

reformulations.difference: The shorthand f_d(n)=n^(2/d-o(1)) is expressed using an existential real-valued error sequence, little-o of the constant-one function, and eventual exact equality. Exact equality here does not assert asymptotic equivalence to n^(2/d) or impose an integrality obstruction.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For each fixed d≥3, the minimization set is nonempty and f_d(n)>0 for n≥2. Little-o of 1 is precisely convergence to 0. Taking logarithms of the eventual equality gives log(f_d(n))/log(n)=2/d-o(n), hence convergence to 2/d. Conversely, that logarithmic limit gives the required error sequence o(n)=2/d-log(f_d(n))/log(n); exponentiating recovers exact equality for n≥2. Values at n=0,1 do not affect either eventual condition. The error and threshold may depend on d, matching the source's explicit fixed-d interpretation. This equivalence for the complete quantified right-hand side was proved in the scratch file.

review.notes: No substantive mathematical misformalization or stale status was found. All declarations in the file were checked (one theorem). /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles and proves the boundary values f_3(0)=f_3(1)=0 and f_3(2)=1, positivity for all d≥3 and n≥2, the universal-lower-bound characterization of the minimum, and the logarithmic-growth equivalence, without sorry dependencies. The problem page and its complete LaTeX text were accessible through public text renderings; forum comments could not be retrieved because of rate limiting. SoVu08's full text was paywalled, but its publisher abstract was read; this does not leave the sole declared conjecture unresolved against the available sources. The reviewed file matches its committed blob and was not modified.
